key_insight: An adaptive reinforcement-learning controller can learn measurement-and-feedback policies from partial experimental data to prepare target quantum states without requiring full state knowledge.
engineering_relevance: The approach is hardware-compatible for quantum simulators and processors because it uses only observable measurement histories and one-shot energy estimates instead of full-state reconstruction.
method: Use reinforcement learning under partial observability to select the next measurement operator and feedback action in real time.
Train with a stochastic terminal reward based on randomly sampled Hamiltonian terms, yielding an unbiased energy estimator.
Apply the learned protocol to ground-state preparation and entangled-state generation tasks.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports demonstrations on ground-state preparation for the Bose-Hubbard model and on GHZ-state generation, indicating task validation on representative quantum benchmarks.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and stability of measurement outcomes and on the scalability of training under experimental noise and limited observability.
paper_title: Experiment-compatible measurement--feedback quantum state preparation with reinforcement learning
